about: One billing_model name set for both libraries (Python ab0t-quota 0.7.3 / Go ab0t-quota-go v0.3.2). Before, the Python library accepted capacity_only, consumption_only, subscription_with_credits, subscription_unlock_only (+ experimental subscription_with_overage, seat_based, metered) and the Go library accepted consumption_only, subscription_unlock_only, subscription_with_credits, free_tier, enterprise (+ experimental metered_billing, one_time_purchase), so a config written for one runtime was refused or misread by the other. `canonical` is the one name set and what each name MEANS. `aliases` are the other library's names for the same meaning: both libraries accept them and print `alias_warning_template`. A name is an alias only when the two libraries run it the same way (free_tier and enterprise had no rule of their own in the Go library: exactly capacity_only; metered_billing and metered are both experimental with no runtime). Experimental names are refused unless `experimental_env`=true, except the names in `go_grace.names`, which the Go library used to accept with an 'unknown' warning: it keeps accepting them with `go_grace.warning_template` until its next minor release (a refusal of a config that started before is a breaking change), while the Python library refuses them as it always did. `cases` hold one tier each: `python` / `go` = ok | refused at load; `warnings_python` / `warnings_go` = which shared texts each library prints for the tier, in order (alias | go_grace | never_fires). `never_fires_warning_template` is printed by both libraries for a credit_grant whose trigger no runtime fires. Byte-identical copy in ab0t-quota/tests/ and ab0t-quota-go/testdata/.

canonical.name: capacity_only
canonical.short_meaning: limits only: the tier itself moves no money
canonical.meaning: Quota limits only. The tier itself moves no money: a price is informational and a credit_grant is the only money it can cause. The default when billing_model is absent.

canonical.name: consumption_only
canonical.short_meaning: pay as you go from a prepaid balance
canonical.meaning: Pay as you go: usage is charged to a prepaid balance. No recurring price.

canonical.name: subscription_with_credits
canonical.short_meaning: a recurring price that includes credit
canonical.meaning: A recurring price whose paid invoice grants credit (credit_grant with trigger subscription_invoice_paid).

canonical.name: subscription_unlock_only
canonical.short_meaning: a recurring price that unlocks limits, no included credit
canonical.meaning: A recurring price that unlocks the tier's limits; no credit_grant.

canonical.name: metered
canonical.short_meaning: experimental: no runtime in either library yet
canonical.meaning: Pure metered billing. Experimental: no runtime path in either library yet.

canonical.name: seat_based
canonical.short_meaning: experimental: no runtime in either library yet
canonical.meaning: Price per seat. Experimental: no runtime path in either library yet.

canonical.name: subscription_with_overage
canonical.short_meaning: experimental: no runtime in either library yet
canonical.meaning: A bundle plus pay-for-the-excess. Experimental: no runtime path in either library yet.

canonical.name: one_time_purchase
canonical.short_meaning: experimental: no runtime in either library yet
canonical.meaning: A one-time purchase. Experimental: no runtime path in either library yet.

alias_warning_template: tier "{tier_id}": billing_model "{name}" is another name for "{canonical}" ({short_meaning}); both libraries accept it — write "{canonical}" to silence this warning

go_grace.warning_template: tier "{tier_id}": billing_model "{name}" is experimental and has no runtime in either library yet; the Python library refuses it unless AB0T_QUOTA_ALLOW_EXPERIMENTAL_BILLING_MODELS=true, and this library will too from its next minor release — until then this tier runs as limits only

unknown_name.go: ok, with the existing warning: tier "{tier_id}": unknown billing_model "{name}" — none of its cross-field rules apply

never_fires_warning_template: tier "{tier_id}": credit_grant.trigger "scheduled_period_start" is accepted but neither library fires it yet — this grant is never given (no periodic refill happens); use "signup", or grant the credit yourself through billing
